description: Find orders — the same rows as Manage → Orders. Answers 'show me order 1042', 'what did we sell on Saturday', 'are there parked orders', 'orders rung up by Maria', 'orders over $500 at the King Street shop'. Filter by receipt number, status, source, employee, customer, product, date window, order total, outlet or station. Results are ALWAYS newest first — there is no other sorting, so a "biggest order" question needs the amount filter, not paging. Search matches the receipt number and the order id ONLY, never customer names or product names: for those, pass customerIds from get_customers or productIds from get_products. One row per order with its total; for what is INSIDE an order — line items, payments, refunds, notes — call get_order with the id from here. For how much the business took over a period use get_financial_summary or get_sales_breakdown instead of adding these rows up.

customerIds.description: Customer ids from get_customers, not names

employeeIds.description: Employee ids — from get_employee_sales, not names

endDate.description: Only orders created at or before this ISO 8601 moment

maxTotal.description: Maximum order total in MINOR units (cents)

minTotal.description: Minimum order total in MINOR units (cents), e.g. 50000 for $500

outlets.description: Outlet ids. Combined with stations by OR

productIds.description: Product ids from get_products — matches orders containing them

search.description: Receipt number or order id. Does NOT match customer or product names

startDate.description: Only orders created at or after this ISO 8601 moment

stations.description: Station ids. Combined with outlets by OR

status.description: Final POS statuses: "completed", "refunded", "partial-refund", "parked". WooCommerce orders keep their own ("processing", "on-hold", "pending", "cancelled", "failed") — pass "other" to match every status outside the four Final POS ones

name: hub_get_orders
title: List orders
